source.title: Towards Explainable Convolutional Features for Music Audio Modeling
source.authors: Anna K. Yanchenko; Mohammadreza Soltani; Robert J. Ravier; Sayan Mukherjee; V. Tarokh

record.file_problem: not stated; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Measures representation similarity across different initializations of the same architectures, bearing on convergence across seeds. It uses linear CKA rather than directly identifying shared features or subspaces.
record.gate_note: The relevant results compare trained representations across initializations. Classification accuracy, deep-to-hand-crafted-feature comparisons, and alternate similarity measures for deep-to-hand-crafted comparisons are not rows for the claim: they do not measure convergence between independently trained model representations. The text also cites prior convergent-learning work, but cited results are not recorded here.
record.test_reason: Appendix F.1 measures linear CKA between conv3 (and, for NSynth, per-layer) features of the same CNN architecture trained from 5 different initializations. This bears directly on V3. The method is CKA rather than unit matching, and the setting is small CNNs on music audio mel-spectrograms. The paper's main focus is deep-vs-hand-crafted feature similarity, which is not a test of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase describes only the appendix seed finding. The paper's main conclusion is that convolutional features are robust across tasks, and that earlier-layer features closely resemble hand-crafted wavelet and signal-processing features even untrained. On seeds, the authors state that features are highly similar but not identical across initializations, so multiple initializations should be used.
record.recipe_differences: Uses linear CKA to compare learned representations across initializations; the text does not describe an explicit replication of the cited convergent-learning method.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear CKA between conv3 features of different architectures trained on the same data (Fig. 45; Regular vs Deformable by layer, Fig. 49). 1dT is least similar to the other architectures; Regular is similar to Deformable and Dilated. These are figure-only, with no scale dimension.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained architectures on the same task and data share representations to a degree that depends on architecture design (cross-architecture convergence without scale).

record.problems: For the relevant initialization comparisons, numerical similarity values are presented only in figures and no uncertainty estimates are stated. The reported qualitative finding is limited to the tested CNN architectures, layers, datasets, and initializations.

untested.parts: Whether individual units or bases differ while features or subspaces are shared. The study uses only whole-layer linear CKA, with no unit matching or subspace analysis. Seed comparisons are limited to 5 seeds of small 3-layer CNNs on audio. Per-layer seed comparisons are reported for NSynth only.
Alternate similarity measures are applied only to deep-vs-hand-crafted comparisons, not to model-to-model convergence.
No analysis of plateaus or of the causes of alignment.

missing.what: Cross-architecture linear CKA at conv3 (Regular, Deformable, Dilated, 1dF, 1dT), averaged over initializations, for all three datasets.
missing.locator: Section F.2, Figure 45; Section F.4, Figure 49
missing.versions: none (cross-architecture convergence without scale; would bear on V1 only with a scale axis)

record.verdict_notes: The cross-seed result is a secondary appendix check, not the paper's aim. All values are figure-only with no numbers or uncertainty. Ties between the earlier-layer state and the cross-seed text rest on the qualitative phrase 'differ more for the earlier and later layers'; conv3 is said to be highly similar yet also grouped with the layers that differ more. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep testing whether alignment rises as models grow or improve; the study does not test convergence across different data, objectives, or modalities.
No paired image-caption or other vision-language representation comparison.
Tests similarity across initializations for specified CNN architectures and datasets, but does not identify shared interpretable features or directly establish shared subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
Does not test recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Alternate similarity measures are compared for deep-to-hand-crafted-feature similarity, not convergence between independently trained models; no OOD or neighbour-setting comparison is reported.
Does not assess whether model-to-model alignment plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives explain it.
